messages.speaker: River
messages.text: You picked a great spot for this. Joggers every ten seconds, wind throwing napkins around, real private. I came over, didn't I.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: You came over now. Earlier you vanished between the potato salad and dessert. Then explain why you disappeared.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: Something came up, that's all. I handled it and came back.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: You always do this. Half a sentence, then act like everyone else is making a scene for noticing.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: I didn't say that. Can we not do this out here? Every other person on this path keeps looking over.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Out here, in the car, over text, it's always the same answer. You leave, hours go by, and then I'm supposed to accept 'something came up.'

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: It wasn't hours. And I wasn't off screwing around, if that's what you're trying to get at. I had to go deal with something.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Then give me the order. Who called, when did you leave, and why couldn't you say one clear sentence before peeling out of the driveway?

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: My phone started blowing up, I walked out, I drove, and by the time it settled down there was already a hundred missed assumptions waiting for me. That's the order.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: That's not an explanation, that's a fog machine. If you didn't want to sit through lunch with everyone picking at you, you could've just said that.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: You really want the clean version? Fine. I stepped out because I couldn't stand there answering ten questions at once.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: So that's it. If you just bailed because you didn't want to deal with us, say that.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: Look at this. Hospital number, three calls, and these messages. I left because I thought Mom's scan had gone bad, and by the time they corrected it, everyone was already upset.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: What? Let me see that again. They said complication and then took it back?

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: Tech flagged the wrong chart, then someone finally fixed it after I was halfway there. I parked, called back, sat there getting the runaround, and by then I had six texts asking why I stormed off.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: You could have sent me one of those texts. Just 'hospital' would have changed this whole conversation.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: And then what, your phone goes off at the table, Aunt Denise starts demanding updates, and suddenly the whole pavilion is talking like something already happened? It was a false alarm. I wasn't turning that into a family announcement.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: No, I get why you didn't broadcast it. But leaving me standing there with everyone asking where you went made me sound like an idiot covering for you.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: Yeah. That part landed badly. Next time, if it's that kind of thing, you'll get a message before I start the car.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Okay. Do that, and I won't fill in the blanks this fast. Is Mom definitely fine now?

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: Can you give me a minute before you take that bag out? I won't keep you long. I just need to say one thing.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Then say it. I've still got the bathroom box and those frames by the fridge. Whatever this is, just make it quick.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: I know. I saw the labels. That's why I waited until your mom went upstairs.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: You picked a great time, standing in the kitchen doorway with an envelope like you're serving papers. Are you blocking me for a reason?

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: No. Move past me if you want. I just didn't want you hearing this later from someone else.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Hearing what, exactly? Because the suspense isn't helping your case.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: I got something in the mail this week. I should've said it sooner, but every time I tried, there were three other people in here and a stack of dishes between us.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: If you're leaving too, just say it. You don't need a whole lead-in.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: It was an offer out of state, but I turned it down. I stayed because I didn't want to disappear on you or your family right now.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: You turned it down. For this house. For all of this.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: Don't make it into a tab. I'm not handing you that letter so you owe me anything. I just didn't want you walking out of here thinking I was already halfway gone.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: I wasn't keeping score. It just... sounded like the opposite of what I was bracing for. You standing there with that folded up like evidence didn't exactly help.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: It is evidence, a little. Not for you to do something with. For once, I wanted there to be one thing in this room that meant exactly what it said.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: You always did wait until the last possible second. And then act surprised when people fill in the blanks for you. Still... thanks for saying it before somebody's aunt turned it into gossip over potato salad.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: I can help with the boxes tomorrow, or not. Same with your uncle's appointments and the landlord forms. You can text me if you need an extra set of hands.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Tomorrow, the boxes in the hall, not my room. And no rearranging labels because you think your system is better. If that works, then text first.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: You picked the loudest coffee shop in the neighborhood. If this paper is bad news, at least the espresso machine can drown it out.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: It's close by, and they had a table. I just want your take on this before I answer the landlord.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: That sounds suspiciously adult of you. Let me guess: columns, arrows, maybe one box circled hard enough to tear the page.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Pretty much. He bumped the rent again, so I wrote out what it looks like split two ways, and I pulled a couple nearby listings in case this place stops making sense.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Landlords love a springtime cash grab. We could always reject the whole system, buy a van, and become impossibly interesting people.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: You say that every time a bill shows up. Does this still make sense for us, though?

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Depends what 'sense' means. The number's not cute, but nothing is right now, and every other place probably comes with mystery plumbing and a raccoon superintendent.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: I circled the monthly total there. If we stay, that's what it comes to each, and if we don't, I need to start calling places now.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: You're doing a whole strategic campaign over one lease renewal. Maybe don't let a landlord set the pace for your entire week.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: It's not my whole week. I just need a yes or no from you, because that changes what I say back.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Why not ask for a few extra days and keep options open? No medal gets handed out for answering first.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: I need to tell the landlord this week if we're renewing together. That's why I brought it here instead of leaving it on the kitchen counter.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: I should have told you already, but I accepted a job in Portland and I'll be moving out. The start date's in two months.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Portland. So all of this, and you've been sitting there making van jokes while I work out next year's rent on a napkin. When did this happen?

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Last week, officially. I kept waiting for a cleaner moment, and then this showed up between the coffee cups. I'll cover my part through the notice period, and I'll help find someone if you want to keep the place.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: I need the exact dates tonight, and I need to know whether the landlord can approve a replacement that fast. Send me whatever paperwork you signed, or at least the timeline, so I can stop guessing.

messages.speaker: Drew
messages.text: Why do you have that? That's my notebook. You were just standing here by the lockers with it like you were waiting for me.

messages.speaker: Sage
messages.text: Lower your voice. It's not what you think. I was going to give it back between bells.

messages.speaker: Drew
messages.text: Then why is it open? And why are you holding it like that? Just say what you were doing.

messages.speaker: Sage
messages.text: I wasn't doing anything weird. You don't need to make this a whole corridor scene. Let me explain it properly.

messages.speaker: Drew
messages.text: You always say that right before some technical excuse. If there was nothing in there, you could've started with that. Instead you went with 'it's not what you think.'

messages.speaker: Sage
messages.text: Because you came up swinging the second you saw it. I got two words out and you were already acting like I'd done something criminal. Can you stop interrupting for five seconds?

messages.speaker: Drew
messages.text: I'm asking because it's mine. You don't just end up with my stuff and then talk around it. People are literally walking by and staring now.

messages.speaker: Sage
messages.text: They're staring because you're making it loud. I wasn't trying to keep it from you. I was trying to hand it over before next period.

messages.speaker: Drew
messages.text: Then hand it over. Unless there's a reason you don't want me seeing the first page.

messages.speaker: Sage
messages.text: Seriously? Fine. Since apparently that's where your mind went, look at it.

messages.speaker: Drew
messages.text: You wrote in it? Wow. So there is a first-page surprise.

messages.speaker: Sage
messages.text: Mr. Collins gave this to me after class because you left it in the science room. I only wrote this note telling you to keep it in your bag.

messages.speaker: Drew
messages.text: Oh. So that's what this is. You could've said Mr. Collins a lot earlier.

messages.speaker: Sage
messages.text: I was about to, until you jumped straight to accusations. 'Why do you have that' wasn't exactly a calm opening. Next time, maybe let me finish one sentence.

messages.speaker: Drew
messages.text: Yeah, okay. I saw you clutching it and doing that pause, and it looked bad. Sorry for coming in hot.

messages.speaker: Sage
messages.text: And maybe don't leave your notebook in a lab again. I wasn't trying to become your lost-and-found desk. Just keep it in your bag like the note says.

messages.speaker: Drew
messages.text: Fair. Thanks for bringing it over instead of leaving it with the office. And thanks for not writing anything worse than that lecture on the front page.

messages.speaker: Sage
messages.text: You're welcome. Now get to class before you lose it again on the way there. And maybe try not to assume the worst of me in under three seconds.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: You barely touched your drink. If this place is too loud, we can go somewhere else. What happened?

messages.speaker: Hayden
messages.text: No, it's fine. I just needed to talk this through with someone. Work has been messing with my head all week.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Okay. We can think through your options. Is this about the project load, or are you at the point where you're thinking about leaving?

messages.speaker: Hayden
messages.text: I don't know how much longer I can do this the way it's been going. Every day feels like one more thing piled on top of the last. And then something happens and you're just supposed to smile through it.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Then maybe don't just push through it. Have you thought about talking to management or updating your resume, just so you have some leverage? Sometimes having a plan makes the whole thing less impossible.

messages.speaker: Hayden
messages.text: Right. A plan. Because apparently everything at work turns into a neat little next step. That's kind of the problem.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: I'm not trying to make it neat. I'm just saying if someone's making your week hell, there are only so many moves on the board. Did your manager say something, or is this more about the team in general?

messages.speaker: Hayden
messages.text: It's not just 'the team in general.' It's when something lands badly and everybody acts like it's normal, like you're not supposed to care. Then if you do care, you look dramatic.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: If it's that bad, you don't have to wait until it blows up. You could ask for a one-on-one, lay out what's not working, and see how they respond. If they brush it off, then you know what that tells you.

messages.speaker: Hayden
messages.text: You keep skipping to the exit signs. Maybe I wasn't asking for a strategy memo over coffee.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Okay. Then tell me which part I'm missing. You said you needed to talk it through, so I figured this was about choosing what to do next.

messages.speaker: Hayden
messages.text: I'm upset because our manager thanked you for the client deck I stayed late to finish, and you started giving me advice like I was just deciding whether to leave.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Wait. That deck? I thought you only cleaned up a couple slides before it went out. I didn't know you were there that late, and I shouldn't have jumped straight into fixing mode.

messages.speaker: Hayden
messages.text: I wasn't looking for a five-step plan. I just didn't want to sit here acting like that didn't sting. Hearing you talk about resumes while I'm trying to swallow that was rough.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Yeah. That's on me. I should've asked what happened before I started laying out options, and I should not have let that thank-you land without checking where the work actually came from.

messages.speaker: Hayden
messages.text: I kept thinking if I said it out loud, it would sound petty. But it wasn't about a line in a meeting. It was the whole staying late, fixing the mess, then sitting there while your name got attached to it.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: That doesn't sound petty. It sounds like your work got handed to someone else, and I was sitting in the wrong seat for that. Tell me what would help now—do you want me to clear it up with our manager, or do you want me to just stay here and hear the rest first?

messages.speaker: Hayden
messages.text: The second one first. Just... let it be ugly for a minute without turning it into an action item. After that, we can figure out what to do.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: Long line at the desk for this hour. If you're here for the conference block, it moves faster once the couple with the silver suitcases is done. You can set that folder on the side table if your arm gets tired.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: Thanks. I think I can survive another minute with it. Actually, while I'm trapped in lobby limbo, can I get your take on something about the panel setup?

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: Of course. As you know, that setup usually works best when the moderator keeps the frame tight and the speakers stay in sequence. It saves everyone from the usual drift.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: Right. I'm still deciding how I feel about the organizer's format versus something looser. You seemed like someone who'd have a read on where it works and where it doesn't.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: The proposed format is cleaner, especially with mixed audiences. People say they want spontaneity, but then the session turns into three separate talks and a rushed Q and A. The organizer's version prevents that.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: That makes sense. I was wondering whether the tighter structure keeps things from feeling too managed. Some panels get a little bloodless when every answer lands in the same shape.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: Only if the panelists can't carry nuance inside the structure. A good moderator can make it feel natural while still protecting the pacing. Given the crowd this conference draws, I'd rather have a format that doesn't depend on luck.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: So you'd put reliability over the chance of a livelier exchange. I can see the appeal there. I haven't had enough of these to know which tradeoff people remember afterward.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: Most people remember whether it felt coherent. And if this is the same proposal that's been circulating, the sequence already solves half the problems before anyone walks onstage. There isn't much reason to reinvent it at the last minute.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: When you put it that way, it sounds pretty settled. I thought there might be more room for judgment in it. Have many people landed in the same place?

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: From what I understood, yes. That's why I figured this was more about confirming the practical choice than reopening the whole question. Once the pieces are in place, the straightforward option usually wins for good reason.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: I actually haven't heard anyone's recommendation yet, so I'm trying to decide from scratch. That's partly why I came over. You sounded like you were picking up in the middle of something.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: Ah. Then I started three steps ahead. I was told notes had already gone around, so I answered as if mine was already on the table.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: That clears up the tone, at least. I was trying to figure out whether you were weighing options or steering me toward one. Those aren't quite the same conversation.

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: Fair point. For what it's worth, I do lean toward the organizer's format, but not because it's the only respectable choice. It just handles uneven speakers and tight timing better than the looser version.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: That's more useful. If it's a preference and not a verdict, I can place it properly. What would make you switch sides, if anything?

messages.speaker: River
messages.text: If the moderator had real authority and the panelists already knew each other's rhythms, I'd loosen it. Or if the goal were friction rather than clarity. But for a room full of people meeting each other for the first time, structure covers a lot.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: Okay. I'll probably ask around a bit more, but that gives me something solid to compare against. And if the desk ever frees up, I owe you a coffee for rescuing the wait.

messages.speaker: Parker
messages.text: You dragged me onto a bench five feet from the walking path, so this had better survive joggers and dogs. What's with the phone?

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: My cousin texted twenty minutes ago. There's an opening at his startup, decent pay, actual benefits, and he'd want an answer fast. I know how that sounds, but objectively it makes more sense.

messages.speaker: Parker
messages.text: You came out here with bullet points ready. That's usually when you want someone to nod at the end. What happened to the school?

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: The school is still there. They want my paperwork by Monday, but this came in first, and the timing's ridiculous. I just need to know if this sounds crazy.

messages.speaker: Parker
messages.text: Crazy isn't the word I'd use. Convenient, maybe. So what do you actually want, not what looks right?

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: Why does everyone act like practical automatically means hollow? It's not like I'd be joining some evil empire; it's a small team, I'd learn a lot, and I'd stop living off substitute hours and optimism.

messages.speaker: Parker
messages.text: Nobody said evil empire. You keep pitching it like you're on a panel, though. Salary, timing, growth, benefits—anything in there that's yours and not just easy to defend at dinner?

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: Mine? Fine. I like that they want me now, not after three rounds and a committee vote. And yeah, it would be nice not to spend the next year pretending ramen is a personality trait.

messages.speaker: Parker
messages.text: That's still about being picked and about not having to explain yourself. You've talked about teaching for months. Not the paycheck, the actual classrooms.

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: I know what I said. That's why this is such a mess, because if I switch now then apparently I'm unserious, and if I don't switch then I'm ignoring something that's right in front of me. There isn't a clean version.

messages.speaker: Parker
messages.text: Then stop hunting for a clean version. Pick the one you can stand behind when nobody claps for it. If you've already got the offer and you're just asking me to bless it, that's not really asking.

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: I haven't told anyone else because I'm scared I'll pick wrong and look fake either way. Happy? That's the part I left out.

messages.speaker: Parker
messages.text: That's different. You made it sound like a spreadsheet with a pulse, and I was getting ready to throw it back at you. Looking fake to who?

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: My parents, the people at the school, everyone I've been talking to for the last year, probably me too. If I take the startup, it looks like I only liked teaching until a shinier thing showed up. If I don't, and six months from now I'm miserable and broke, that looks pretty fake too.

messages.speaker: Parker
messages.text: People will build a story no matter what you do. That's free and unavoidable. The part you actually get to choose is whether you're walking into a classroom because you want that life now, or because backing out would be embarrassing.

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: Okay. Then try this with me: which regret is louder later, passing on the startup and wondering, or taking it and always side-eyeing myself every time I say I cared about teaching?

messages.speaker: Parker
messages.text: Which one keeps showing up even when nobody's around to witness it? And strip out your cousin, your parents, the school, all of them. On a boring Tuesday, which job still looks like yours?

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: The annoying part is I know exactly why that question helps. The classroom still shows up when I do that, just with a lot less polish around it. So maybe the real problem isn't that the offer is better; it's that the other one asks more from me right away.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: This place is quieter than I expected. You can actually hear the ice hit the glass in here. I kind of like that.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: It's easier to talk when we don't have to compete with a crowd. And since we've seen each other a few times now, I figured a place like this made sense. The food's good, too, which helps.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: You picked well. Even the lighting looks like it's trying not to interrupt anybody. So, this sounded like more than just dinner when you texted.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: I think it's better to be upfront about expectations. We've gotten along easily, and I'd rather talk clearly than drift and guess. What are you looking for long term?

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Long term is a pretty polished phrase for halfway through a drink. I don't know, I guess I look for something that doesn't feel temporary. Something that doesn't turn into a checklist.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: Fair. I'm not talking about a checklist for the sake of it. I mean things like whether two people want the same pace, the same level of consistency, the same kind of effort.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: So you like to have things figured out. That can be useful. It can also make the other person wonder when the verdict comes in.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: I'd rather not waste anyone's time by being vague. If I keep showing up, texting, making plans, that should count for something. I'm asking because I take this seriously.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Maybe. Sometimes people say serious things in a very careful voice right before they explain why something won't work. It starts to sound neat and finished.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: That's not what I'm doing. I'm asking because I want to know if you'd want the kind of relationship that's actually steady, not half in and half out. The practical part matters if you're trying to build anything real.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: You keep saying it like a plan you're presenting. Same pace, consistency, effort, practical part. You sound like you've already made up your mind.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: I kind of have—I asked you here because I want to see if we're heading toward being together, not because I'm losing interest. I've been trying to make that sound solid, and apparently it came out colder than I meant. This wasn't supposed to be an exit speech.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Oh. That's... different from how it was landing over here. It sounded a lot like you were arranging the plates before bad news.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: No bad news. I like being here with you, and I don't usually do well with hinting my way through something important. If I came off like I was evaluating you from across the table, that's on me.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: I can work with direct a lot better when it comes with that part. Otherwise it gets easy to fill in the blanks with the worst version. I wasn't exactly making it easy to read me either.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: Then let's stop making each other guess so much. I'd like to keep seeing you and do it in a way that isn't casual or blurry. If you want, we can start there and leave the spreadsheets out of it.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: This place is louder than I remembered. They keep calling names and nobody hears them the first time. Your coffee's going cold.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: I've had colder. Eat the rest of that pastry before it turns into a brick. So, how bad was the week really, once you got past Thursday?

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: Thursday was only part of it. The labs, the group work, the way everything stacks up at once. It feels different when every assignment depends on three other people.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: Group work is miserable half the time, but it passes. One rough semester can make everything look bigger than it is. You've already built a lot where you are.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: If there were another setup, something less crowded and less... constant, would you count that as giving up? Or just picking differently?

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: I'd count it based on why. Sometimes changing lanes helps, and sometimes it just trades one headache for another. The current program has structure, teachers who know you, and people keeping an eye on how you're doing.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: What if the structure is part of the problem? Not the classes exactly, more the way every hour is already spoken for. Some people do better when nobody is hovering.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: Some people say that right when things get demanding. Then later they wish they'd waited a bit before blowing up the whole plan. Have you actually looked at what the other option would expect from you day to day?

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: What if I had. What if it wasn't just some random idea from a bad week. Would that change the speech?

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: I'm not giving a speech. I'm saying there are reasons not to throw away a solid path because this month has been ugly. You do not need to rush into some big switch just because this semester feels hard.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: I already said yes to the transfer program yesterday. I wanted to tell you in person because I needed to know whether you'd hear me or just talk me out of it.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: Yesterday. And we're getting to that now, over lukewarm coffee. You had the whole thing settled while I was sitting here listing reasons like none of it had happened.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: You started listing them before I got through two sentences. Every time I tried to get near it, you were already at 'one rough semester' and 'don't blow up the plan.' So I kept waiting to see if there was room for anything else.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: All right. That's fair, even if I don't love hearing it. Start from the beginning and leave out the part where I'm supposed to guess.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: The principal called me in Monday after my advisor flagged how the independent study track works. Smaller load, more one-on-one check-ins, fewer group projects, and time to pace the research piece properly. I said yes because the first time anyone described next semester, it sounded like something I could actually do well in instead of just survive.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: That sounds a lot more thought-through than I gave you credit for. I wish I'd been part of it before the answer went back, but that's not the same as saying it was the wrong answer. What happens next, and where do I fit without crowding you?

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: There's an orientation next week and forms after that. You could come to the meeting if you want, or just help me look over the schedule afterward. I don't need a rescue team; I just don't want this to turn into a cold war every time I choose something first.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: No cold war. Send me the time for the orientation, and I'll keep my mouth shut long enough to hear the whole thing before I start in with advice. And eat the pastry now, because if we're doing this your way, I'm at least winning on that part.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: Alex. Look at this for a second. I've got your thread open, and the barista can yell all they want.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: I saw it. You didn't need to catch me at the pickup counter.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: You weren't exactly making yourself available anywhere else. Eleven texts, one call, and then nothing. Meanwhile people from the old office are asking me what happened.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: It wasn't like that. And maybe keep your voice down.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: Then tell me what it was like. Because from where I was standing, it looked pretty simple: I sent something urgent, and you let it sit while I cleaned it up.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: You already sound like you've got the whole story. Me adding anything now probably won't help.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: Don't do that clipped one-line thing with me. Dana said everyone over there thinks you bailed and left me covering for both of us. I'm not carrying that around because you decided silence was good enough.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: Dana talks too much. And I didn't ask you to cover for me.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: No, you just left me with the calls and the questions. You know what that sounds like when nobody can reach you. It sounds like exactly what it looked like.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: You're acting like I vanished on purpose. I didn't.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: You left me to explain it alone. So if there's some version where that isn't what happened, now would be a great time.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: I muted the thread because I was at the cardiology clinic with my dad all morning; I was going to answer after. Here. That's the check-in notification from 8:12, and the follow-up alert came in an hour later.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: I didn't know that. Dana made it sound like you just looked at the messages and tossed your phone aside. Why mute it, though?

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: Because the screen kept lighting up while I was trying to hear what the doctor was saying. I figured I'd answer once I had something besides half a sentence and a hallway. That part clearly aged well.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: People filled in the blanks fast. I had three separate calls before lunch, and none of them were kind. I'm not taking all of that by myself again.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: Fair. Next time you'll get a short heads-up, even if that's all there is. And Dana can hear the rest from me instead of from a table full of spectators.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: Cameron, wait a sec. This was under my tray, and your handwriting is all over this page. The whole lunch line is moving and I just want to know what happened.

messages.speaker: Cameron
messages.text: I already told you, I just found it. You don't have to come over here waving it around. Put it down before somebody dumps their soda on it.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: I'm not waving it around, I'm pointing at the note inside. Why is there a weird message in my own notebook saying it was found by the library? That doesn't exactly explain itself.

messages.speaker: Cameron
messages.text: Because that's where I said I found it. What else do you want me to add to that? People are staring already.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: They're staring because you're answering like I asked whether you forged government documents. It's a notebook, but it's also my notebook. The story just sounds trimmed down.

messages.speaker: Cameron
messages.text: Maybe because it doesn't need a whole speech in the middle of the cafeteria. I handed it back, didn't I? Can we just drop it and sit down?

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: That would work better if the note wasn't inside the middle of my pages like some tiny cover story. If you picked it up off the floor, why write that at all? That's the part that makes this weird.

messages.speaker: Cameron
messages.text: You keep saying it like I was digging through your stuff for fun. I wasn't. And maybe I wrote it because I didn't want this exact scene happening over lunch.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: I didn't say you were digging through anything. I'm saying the explanation keeps changing shape every time I ask one question. If there's one more piece, just say that piece.

messages.speaker: Cameron
messages.text: Easy for you to say when you're the one standing there with evidence in your hand. You came over fast enough that half the table looked up. So forgive me if this doesn't feel casual.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: Fine, not casual. But I'm not trying to do a courtroom thing in front of french fries and chocolate milk. I saw the note, I saw your writing, and none of it matched the quick version.

messages.speaker: Cameron
messages.text: Because the quick version sounded cleaner. That's all. Some things look worse out loud than they were.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: Then give me the messy version, because the clean one is doing you zero favors. Right now it sounds like you're trying to beat the question instead of answer it. I'd rather hear the awkward truth than the polished one.

messages.speaker: Cameron
messages.text: Keep your voice down. I did have your notebook for a minute before lunch. I only copied the assignment title because I missed it, and I wrote that library note because I didn't want people to think I took it from your bag.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: Oh. That is... a lot more specific than where this was headed in my head. You could've just asked me for the title, but that's not the same thing as whatever this was starting to look like.

messages.speaker: Cameron
messages.text: Yeah, well, by the time I had it, asking would've made its own problem. Then the note seemed smarter for about thirty seconds. It didn't exactly improve with daylight.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: No, the fake library breadcrumb was not your strongest draft. But missing the heading and grabbing the notebook for that makes actual sense. I wasn't trying to make you look like some criminal mastermind.

messages.speaker: Cameron
messages.text: I shouldn't have taken it without saying anything. And the note was dumb. Sorry for making it look sketchier than it was.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: Okay. Next time just tap my shoulder or steal the homework title from my paper while I'm opening ketchup, same result and fewer mystery notes. We can retire the library fiction.

messages.speaker: Cameron
messages.text: Deal. And maybe next time don't charge across the cafeteria holding the exhibit up in the air. Sit down before your fries get cold.

messages.speaker: Phoenix
messages.text: You're blocking the aisle. If you're looking for a seat, that one's open by the stacks. Or was there something else?

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: So you just left me hanging earlier? I had to stand outside the building like an idiot waiting for an answer.

messages.speaker: Phoenix
messages.text: Keep your voice down. And start at the beginning, because that could mean three different things today.

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: You know exactly which one. You could've at least answered instead of disappearing.

messages.speaker: Phoenix
messages.text: Answered what? I've been in lab and then in here with this mess of notes. Can you just tell me what this is about?

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: About not making people chase you for basic coordination. We said we'd figure out whether to meet after class, and then nothing.

messages.speaker: Phoenix
messages.text: We said we'd check in after class, yes. That's not the same as me vanishing on purpose, which is how you're making it sound.

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: Then why am I the one piecing together what happened while you sit here acting like it's minor? One reply would've handled it.

messages.speaker: Phoenix
messages.text: I'm sitting here trying to get you to be specific. If there's a message, say when you sent it instead of circling the point.

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: I texted you right after class and you never answered.

messages.speaker: Phoenix
messages.text: Hold on. Let me see. I never saw this until now—my phone was buried in my bag during lab.

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: Oh. All right, that explains a lot more than what I had in mind.

messages.speaker: Phoenix
messages.text: You came in hot for something that was sitting under a notebook and a pair of goggles. The timestamp's right there.

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: Yeah, I see it. I should've checked before walking over here like that.

messages.speaker: Phoenix
messages.text: Next time, call if it's time-sensitive. My phone goes dead to the world during lab, and apparently that matters more than I thought.

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: Fair. If I don't get a reply, I'll call instead of filling in the blanks and making this a whole scene by the reference desk.

messages.speaker: Phoenix
messages.text: Good plan. And for the record, if I drop something, you'll get an actual message, not silence.

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: Noted. So the meeting question from earlier—are we doing tomorrow after two, or should I stop guessing there too?

messages.speaker: Phoenix
messages.text: Tomorrow after two works. Send it to me, and if you don't get anything back by one-fifteen, call.

messages.speaker: Logan
messages.text: Done. I'll let you get back to your notes before I create another public service announcement for the silent section.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: Hey—sorry. What happened here? I saw this table a little while ago, and these papers were already spread out.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: I was just standing here. I'm not using the laptop or anything.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: Right, okay. It's just—this notebook and the charger looked familiar, so I wanted to check before anything got more awkward.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: If you're asking whether I took somebody's spot, no. I'm here because someone asked me to stay with this for a minute.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: I wasn't trying to make it a whole thing. Mina had been working here earlier, and this looks like her setup.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: Then maybe ask Mina why her stuff got left with me. I didn't set any of this out.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: I'm only asking because people usually don't leave a laptop open in the library unless someone's holding the table. The way it looked from over there, it seemed like you'd settled in.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: Well, that's not what this is. I've been standing here the whole time, and I didn't touch the keyboard.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: Okay. Then whose things are you watching?

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: I'm not claiming any of this. Sam asked me to watch their stuff for five minutes.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: Wait, that's Mina's, not Sam's. That blue notebook is hers—I see it every week.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: Oh. Then either Sam grabbed the wrong table, or I got handed this with half the story missing.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: That makes a lot more sense. Sorry—I came over thinking you had moved into her space and were brushing it off.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: I figured that's what this was about. Sam rushed off toward the printers and said, 'Can you stay here a sec,' so I didn't exactly do a background check on the notebook.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: No, that's fair. Mina might've left her things with Sam, or Sam was saving the table for both of them and said it badly.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: Either way, this probably belongs to both of them more than it belongs to me. If Sam doesn't come back in another minute, you can text Mina and I'll stay put till someone claims it.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: Can we stay here a minute, by the side door? Everyone's almost gone, and I don't want to say this while people are still milling around the chairs. This is hard to say here.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: Of course. We don't have to rush out just because they're stacking up the back rows. What did you want to talk through?

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: I need to know where you stand. Not in some general way, not later over dishes, and not after we get home. Here.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: All right. Then say it plainly, and I'll do the same. I don't want this turning into another careful half-conversation.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: Last week in the hall, after the study group, Martin laughed about people like me and called it honesty. Two others heard it and looked at the floor, and then tonight he was up front shaking hands like nothing happened. I can't keep standing in this room and pretending those things don't count.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: That shouldn't have happened. But before you decide anything final, there may be a way to address it without letting this place become only that moment. I just want to make sure we're not talking past each other.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: That's exactly what I was afraid you would say. Every time something like this happens, it turns into process and patience and giving people room. Meanwhile the person who got named is supposed to keep showing up and singing.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: I'm not asking you to sing through it. I'm trying to understand whether you're asking me what I make of what he said, or whether you're asking what I plan to do. Those aren't the same question.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: They become the same question pretty quickly. If you can still come here after that and call it complicated, then I know enough. I didn't bring this up to win an argument.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: You don't have to sharpen it like that. I've been careful because I thought you were already done with me over this, and I was trying not to make it worse by barging in halfway through what you were saying.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: Done with you isn't what this is. But I can't keep guessing whether you're staying because it's easier, or because you think this kind of thing is survivable if everyone keeps their voice soft enough. I needed an answer before we got back in the car together and acted normal.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: I need you to know I already told the coordinator I may stop coming because what was said here was wrong, and I was afraid you thought I was choosing this place over you. I didn't say anything sooner because every version of the conversation in my head sounded clumsy or late.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: You told the coordinator? Last week? Then all this careful wording wasn't you trying to smooth it over.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: No. I was trying not to step on what you were bringing me, especially here of all places. And when you said you needed to know where I stand, it sounded like there was a line on the floor already.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: I heard you say 'talk this through' and thought I was about to get the keep-the-peace version. Martin didn't just make some vague comment. He said people like me always demand special approval and then called discomfort a sign of faithfulness.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: That's worse than I knew. No wonder you've been going quiet every Sunday afternoon and taking forever before coming in the apartment door. I should have pressed sooner instead of waiting for the right moment to appear on its own.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: I kept thinking if I said it out loud, you'd start listing all the people here who are kind, and then I'd have to sort through that while standing under the stained glass. I didn't have room for that tonight. I just needed this to stop being something I carried alone.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: You're not carrying it alone now. We can tell the coordinator together exactly what was said, or we can be done here without another meeting, but I'm not going to ask you to keep making yourself small for the sake of a bulletin and a familiar routine.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: Together would help, if only so the room doesn't rewrite it by next week. And if we leave, I don't want it to turn into one of those quiet fade-outs where everyone pretends nothing drove us out. I can manage sad; I can't do erased.

messages.speaker: Avery
messages.text: Then we won't do erased. We'll write it down tonight while it's still exact, and tomorrow we can decide whether it goes to the coordinator alone or to the board too. After that, we find somewhere no one mistakes harm for honesty.

messages.speaker: Sutton
messages.text: You pushed your menu away like the answer was obvious, and then you said the employee should have lied for him. In a place full of people paying their bills and following the rules, that lands badly.

messages.speaker: Rowan
messages.text: That is not what I said. I said you cannot judge it without knowing what the person was facing, and maybe we do not need to do this loud enough for the next table to weigh in.

messages.speaker: Sutton
messages.text: Lowering your voice does not fix the point. Either the employee lied on the form or she did not, and if she did, then why are you bending over backward to defend it?

messages.speaker: Rowan
messages.text: Because it is more complicated than a checkbox and a rulebook. If someone is trying to keep a roof over a family member's head or keep a person safe, that matters.

messages.speaker: Sutton
messages.text: It matters after you say it was wrong, not instead of saying it. If you keep making exceptions, the rule means nothing.

messages.speaker: Rowan
messages.text: And if you treat every case the same, then the people inside the case stop existing. There is a difference between a standard and a sentence.

messages.speaker: Sutton
messages.text: Then answer cleanly. Was it wrong for her to lie to the investigator, yes or no?

messages.speaker: Rowan
messages.text: It depends on what she was protecting and what the lie cost. You keep asking for one word as if that makes the situation cleaner than it is.

messages.speaker: Sutton
messages.text: No, I keep asking because every time I ask, you move the line. First it was sympathy, then pressure, now protection; pretty soon anything with a sad backstory gets a pass.

messages.speaker: Rowan
messages.text: That is not fair. You are turning compassion into permission, and those are not the same thing.

messages.speaker: Sutton
messages.text: Then stop circling it. If a person can point to fear or loyalty or need and that softens judgment, what exactly stops the next person from doing the same?

messages.speaker: Rowan
messages.text: Maybe the part where we ask harder questions than whether a rule was broken. Maybe motive, pressure, harm, and alternatives still count even when they do not fit neatly on your side of the receipt.

messages.speaker: Sutton
messages.text: You are making this sound noble when it was still deception. Say the word wrong, Rowan, and then add all the poetry you want after that.

messages.speaker: Rowan
messages.text: I am not defending dishonesty; I am saying I could not condemn someone in that position without asking what they were protecting. Those are different things.

messages.speaker: Sutton
messages.text: What they were protecting. So you are drawing a line between the act and the judgment that follows it. You should have said it that plainly ten minutes ago.

messages.speaker: Rowan
messages.text: I tried, just not in the courtroom style you prefer. Calling something wrong does not require pretending every wrong thing comes from the same place.

messages.speaker: Sutton
messages.text: Fine. Then the act stays wrong, but the person and the circumstances change how hard the response should come down. I can work with that more than I can work with 'it depends' floating around by itself.

messages.speaker: Rowan
messages.text: And I can grant that if everything turns into an exception, standards collapse. I was never arguing for a blank check, only that judgment without context gets cruel fast.

messages.speaker: Sutton
messages.text: Cruel is one risk; drift is the other. If nobody is willing to name the line, people stop seeing it, but I can see why you keep looking at who got pinned under it.

messages.speaker: Rowan
messages.text: Then maybe we are closer than this table made it sound. You keep the line visible, and I will keep asking who is standing there when everyone starts pointing at it.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: You’re going to cut off circulation if you pull those any tighter. Coach already yelled about people sitting that close to the edge of the mat. Got a minute?

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: I heard him. I’m not in anyone’s way. What is it?

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: You’ve been doing that thing where you answer in three words and stare at your hands. Did something happen here, or did I miss something?

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: Nothing happened. You didn’t miss anything. Can this wait until after rounds?

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: If it could, I wouldn’t be standing here with a towel on my shoulder cooling off for no reason. You’ve been off all week, and every time I ask, you give me scraps.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: Maybe I’m just tired. Not everything needs a meeting in the middle of the gym. People are already looking.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: Let them look. I’m not asking for a speech, Jordan. I’m asking why you’ve been acting like this place—or me—did something.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: You’re making it bigger than it is. I came here to train, not explain myself between the jump ropes and the heavy bag.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: That would work better if you’d looked at me once since I walked over. Right now it sounds like you’ve already decided something and you’re just waiting to say it after the fact.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: You seem pretty ready for whatever answer you think is coming. So go ahead and say it instead of circling.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: Fine. I heard Coach mention you checking out Eastside. If you’re mad at me or this place, just say it.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: I’m not mad at you. I only booked one trial because I needed space to think.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: One trial is different from walking out the door. That’s not how the front desk made it sound. You could’ve said that before I had to drag it out of you.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: I know. You came over like I’d packed my stuff and left a note on the lockers. I didn’t want this turning into a whole argument before I even knew what the visit meant.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: I came over because rumors get ugly fast in here, and Coach has the subtlety of a fire alarm. Hearing it from him instead of you was a great touch, though.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: That part’s fair. I should’ve said something before he started talking. I just wanted one thing that wasn’t already being discussed by three people near the water fountain.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: You can try somewhere else. I’m not going to chain you to this mat. Just don’t hand me the cleaned-up version after everyone else gets the preview.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: You get the unpolished version, then. Eastside’s across town, nobody knows me there, and one session sounded quieter than answering questions here before I’d even wrapped my hands.

messages.speaker: Frankie
messages.text: That makes more sense than the story I built from you refusing to look up. Next time, give me one sentence sooner. It saves both of us this whole performance.

messages.speaker: Jordan
messages.text: Next time, I will. And for the record, you can stop standing there like you’re about to deliver a verdict. It makes tying gloves unnecessarily dramatic.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: Hold on, don't move the tray yet. The spill's running along the edge of the table, and your cup tipped when everything shifted.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: Everything shifted because you hit it. My drink was fine until your tray came over and suddenly it's all over your lunch and half this table.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: My tray was already down. Look at where the soda went—it's coming from your side, not mine. Can we just sort out what actually happened before this gets louder?

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: Oh, so now it's about volume? People are looking because my cup ended up in your food and you're standing here explaining the geometry instead of saying you knocked it.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: I'm pointing because it matters. The wet line is right here on the table edge, and your cup slid across, it didn't get swatted sideways.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: You keep doing that, like if you trace enough little lines around the table it'll erase what happened. I saw your arm come in, then my drink went over.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: My arm came in with the tray, yes. That's not the same as hitting your cup. There was a jolt before it moved.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: Convenient jolt. Right when everyone's packed in here and nobody can check it, suddenly there's this invisible shove that clears you.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: It wasn't invisible. Someone behind you clipped the table when they squeezed past. That's why I kept pointing over there.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: Then why not start with that instead of acting like I'm missing some science lesson? From over here it looked pretty direct.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: I did not hit your cup. The student behind you bumped the table, and your drink slid when the trays shifted. See the wet edge here, and the gap behind you where everyone was pushing through?

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: Wait. That guy with the backpack came through there a second before this, didn't he? I thought you were just dodging it.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: He caught the corner and kept moving. I was trying to show you before your sleeve ended up in the soda too.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: Right. Okay, that... tracks more than what I was saying. Sorry for coming at you like that in the middle of lunch rush.

messages.speaker: Reese
messages.text: It's fine. Cafeteria traffic turns one bad step into a whole courtroom scene. Here, take these napkins before the puddle reaches your phone.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: Thanks. And your lunch got wrecked because of my drink, so I'll cover another one if the line isn't impossible. Let's just not do this again with an audience.

messages.speaker: Ellis
messages.text: Why is there an extra charge on here? The food's getting cold while this thing sits in the middle of the table like a dare. That wasn't on the menu, and it sure wasn't mentioned when they dropped the check.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Just look at the line item before you start accusing people. It's printed right there under the subtotal. You don't need to make this louder than it already is.

messages.speaker: Ellis
messages.text: Louder? I'm reading a bill, not flipping a table. 'Service adjustment' could mean anything, and there is no way this belongs on our bill.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: It's on the receipt, Ellis. That usually means it came from somewhere other than a secret plot against you. Maybe pause for two seconds before calling it a scam.

messages.speaker: Ellis
messages.text: There it is. Anything a restaurant prints, you act like it's carved into stone. If they can slap on mystery fees and everyone just shrugs, that's not exactly impressive civilization.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: I'm not saying printed equals sacred. I'm saying maybe don't aim a firing squad at the waitstaff before you've read the whole page. The table next to us doesn't need front-row seats to your consumer crusade.

messages.speaker: Ellis
messages.text: So this is about the audience now. Great. You'd rather I smile, pay it, and let them keep adding charges because heaven forbid somebody at the next table hears a question.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: I'd rather you not barrel straight into blaming people who didn't write the policy. There's a difference between asking a question and gearing up for a performance. You've always skipped that distinction when you get annoyed.

messages.speaker: Ellis
messages.text: Then let's call the manager over right now. One sentence, direct answer, done. Unless the plan is to keep tapping the paper until I magically decide this makes sense.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: You're acting like no explanation could possibly exist. That's the part making this ridiculous. The line is there for a reason whether you like it or not.

messages.speaker: Ellis
messages.text: Then say the reason. You've been doing this little 'it's on the receipt' routine for five minutes. If you've got something real, use words.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Fine. I already asked the server. That charge is the automatic gratuity they added after your joke about walking out got overheard by the manager.

messages.speaker: Ellis
messages.text: What? That was a joke. I said it because we'd been waiting forever for drinks.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: I know what you said it like. They only heard the part about walking out. So when you started in on the receipt, you were yelling at people over something I had already checked.

messages.speaker: Ellis
messages.text: You could've led with that. Instead you went with courtroom tapping and the public-service lecture. No wonder this turned into a whole thing.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Maybe. But every time I tried to get a sentence in, you were halfway to summoning the manager like you wanted a showdown. It's not exactly easy to explain something while you're gearing up to challenge half the room.

messages.speaker: Ellis
messages.text: I'm not calling anyone over now. If that's what happened, then arguing about fraud makes me look ridiculous. Just... leave the receipt here a second.

messages.speaker: Casey
messages.text: Fine. Eat before it gets worse, and when the server comes back, keep it simple. We can finish dinner without making them pay for one bad joke twice.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: The flyer says exactly what they need it to say, and the office closes in forty minutes. Your shoes are right by the couch, so let's not turn the living room into a courtroom. Come on.

messages.speaker: Emerson
messages.text: I read it. That's the problem. You left it on the coffee table like it was just another errand, and it isn't.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: It's not that serious; we just need to handle this. People smooth things over all the time when bills pile up and nobody else steps in.

messages.speaker: Emerson
messages.text: You keep calling it smoothing things over. It says one thing happened when another thing happened, and that crosses a line.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Listen to yourself. Every sentence out of you sounds like you're grading me, and I'm standing here asking for one ride across town, not a sermon.

messages.speaker: Emerson
messages.text: I can't just pretend this is fine. You want me there so it looks cleaner, and you know it.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: I want you there because we're supposed to show up for each other. But you plant yourself by the couch with that paper in your hand like the whole house has to stop until you make your point.

messages.speaker: Emerson
messages.text: You asked for a yes or no before you even answered what I asked. Then you stood by the door jangling the keys like that settled it.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Because we don't have all night, Emerson. Are you coming or not?

messages.speaker: Emerson
messages.text: Why is that the only question you care about? You keep pushing the answer and skipping over what the answer means.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: What it means is this family needs one thing done without everybody making it harder. Sometimes you help first and sort out the fine print later.

messages.speaker: Emerson
messages.text: That's exactly it. The 'fine print' is the part where someone signs something that isn't true, and then everybody acts like the wording did the damage instead of the lie.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: So that's what this is? You stand there and act like I'm dragging you into something filthy, and if you stay home you get to come out clean.

messages.speaker: Emerson
messages.text: If I go with you, I am telling myself that our comfort matters more than being honest, and I can't live with that. I'm not saying that to punish you. I'm saying it because I have to be able to hear my own voice tomorrow.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: You could've said it like that an hour ago. I heard all the clipped little lines and the pointing at the paper, and it sounded like you were putting me on trial.

messages.speaker: Emerson
messages.text: I know it came out sharp. Every time you cut it down to 'just come with me,' it made it sound like the only thing on the table was whether I'd obey.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: It's not only that. When you stay planted and won't even take the keys, it lands like you're stepping away from me, not just from this form.

messages.speaker: Emerson
messages.text: I'm stepping away from the form. You can be angry about that if you want, but I'm not getting in the car for this. I can still sit here when you get back.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: I'm not asking again. I'll figure out something else. Just don't make tonight the only thing we know how to say to each other.

messages.speaker: Emerson
messages.text: I won't. But this stays a no. Leave the flyer here if you want; I'm not changing what it says to me.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Can you turn the TV off if you're not watching it? The flickering is making this worse. I just need a minute.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: The TV is already muted. Is there something you need to tell me about school? You have been circling this all evening.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: It is not exactly what you think. I have just been really tired lately, and mornings have been bad. I did not know how to bring it up.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: Then bring it up plainly. Do not make me drag this out of you. What happened this week?

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: A couple days got messed up. I stayed home once, and another time I got there late and it snowballed. I was going to fix it before it turned into a whole thing.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: Which days, Jesse? Monday, Wednesday, Friday? And do not tell me this is just about oversleeping.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Why are you asking like that? I said I was trying to explain it. Every word I pick sounds wrong the second it comes out.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: Because half-answers are not explanations. If I have to keep guessing, this gets worse, not better. So stop trimming the edges off it.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: You make it sound like I was out doing something stupid. I was in the parking lot one day, and another day I got as far as the bus stop and came back. I was not trying to make a joke out of this.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: I did not say it was a joke. I am asking how many times you were absent and whether anyone at school knows this is bigger than being careless.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: It kept happening. I would get ready, and then right before I had to go in, everything would lock up. I could not make myself walk through the doors.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: Say the whole thing. No shortcuts. I need the truth from you tonight.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: I have been skipping because I panic before I go in. I know how that sounds. I kept thinking if I could just get through one normal day, I would not have to say any of this.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: I already got a call from school, but I am not here to trap you; let us figure out counseling and attendance together. Next time, do not sit alone with this until somebody else phones me first. We can work on the reason and the missed days at the same time.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: They called you already? That is why you kept asking about specific days. I thought this was going to turn into losing my phone and getting watched every second.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: There will be consequences for lying by omission, but I am not starting with a punishment list. Tomorrow we call the counselor back, and we ask what support is actually in place. Then we make a plan for mornings that does not depend on you just forcing it.

messages.speaker: Jesse
messages.text: Okay. I can tell you which days, and I can go with you if you call. I do not want to keep doing this and pretending I can clean it up before anyone notices.

messages.speaker: Quinn
messages.text: Good. Start with the days, then we write down what happens before you leave the house and what happens when you get near the building. We will deal with trust after we deal with what has been stopping you.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: It's loud enough in here that I have to do this now or not at all. Where do you see this going?

messages.speaker: Dakota
messages.text: Straight to the serious question before we finish our drinks? I like being here with you. I just don't want to answer sloppily.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: I'm not grading your wording. I'm asking because we've had a few nights that didn't feel like background noise, and I don't do great with guessing games.

messages.speaker: Dakota
messages.text: I'm not trying to turn it into one. I like spending time with you, and this doesn't feel throwaway to me. I'm just trying to say it in a way that doesn't land wrong.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: That sounds careful to the point of evasive. If you're about to tell me this is fun but that's all, just say that.

messages.speaker: Dakota
messages.text: It's not that simple. And it's not just 'fun' to me. You're making it sound cleaner than it is.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: Cleaner is useful. You go quiet, stare at the glass, and I get handed phrases like 'not that simple'—that usually means I'm hearing the soft version first.

messages.speaker: Dakota
messages.text: Or it means there's something attached to the answer that doesn't fit in a neat sentence. Not everything vague is a dodge.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: Fine. Then give me the attached part. Are you actually interested in this, or am I reading it wrong?

messages.speaker: Dakota
messages.text: I am interested, but I may be moving for a job in about two months, and I didn't know how to tell you without making it sound like I was keeping you at arm's length.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: Okay. That's different from what I thought you were circling around. When did this become real?

messages.speaker: Dakota
messages.text: Real enough to stop feeling hypothetical a little while ago. Real enough that every time we made plans, it sat there at the edge of the table with us.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: And you were going to tell me tonight if I didn't ask? Or was this headed for after another drink and a safer moment?

messages.speaker: Dakota
messages.text: Probably after another drink, which isn't a flattering answer. I kept trying to find a version that didn't sound like an exit speech before anything had even started.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: I can work with inconvenient. I don't work especially well with being managed. Is the move set, or is it still one of those 'if everything lines up' situations?

messages.speaker: Dakota
messages.text: It's close enough that I'd be packing boxes, not making a vision board. There are still final pieces, but not the kind that make this small.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: So the timeline is real, and this wasn't you trying to keep me in the shallow end. That's better, even if it's not exactly what I wanted to hear.

messages.speaker: Dakota
messages.text: You deserved the full picture sooner. I wasn't trying to keep one foot out the door. I just didn't want the first honest thing between us to sound like a warning label.

messages.speaker: Ari
messages.text: It does sound like a warning label, but at least it's on the bottle now. I'm not asking for promises over bar music. I am asking what you'd want us to do with the next two months.

messages.speaker: Dakota
messages.text: Keep being honest, even when it ruins the mood a little. See what this is with the actual facts in the room. And if that makes it too complicated for you, I'd rather hear that than a polished version.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: Hey, there you are. I grabbed the key already, so once they finish up here we can head straight to the elevators. This lobby is nicer than it looked online.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: Yeah. Looks busy. Long trip?

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: Not too bad, I got in early and claimed a chair before that tour group flooded the place. You're traveling light, huh? That little suitcase survived better than mine ever do.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: It does the job. I don't bring much. Check-in usually takes a while?

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: Depends who's at the desk, but we should be up there soon. I put us down already so they don't have to do the whole back-and-forth. Easier that way.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: You talked to them already? Efficient. I still need to sort my part.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: Nothing major, just the usual names and dates. The room's supposed to have a good view, so at least if the AC rattles we get something in return. You can take whichever side works for you.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: I'll see what they have first. Hotels like to switch things around. Better to hear it from the desk.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: Sure, but it's basically set. They handed me this card like ten minutes ago, so unless they've invented a new way to confuse people, we're good. You look wiped out, honestly, so getting upstairs fast might save you.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: I'm fine. I'd rather not skip steps. If there's paperwork, I'd rather do it now.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: You're very by-the-book today. It's one front desk, not customs. Come on, once they nod, we dump the bags and figure out food.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: A nod for what, exactly? You've been talking like everything's already arranged. I haven't heard much from anyone except you.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: Next guest, please. Oh, perfect timing. Since Kai already added Alex to the room earlier, I just need confirmation.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: I never agreed to that. If there's another room available, I'd like that instead. Separate booking is fine.

messages.speaker: Kai
messages.text: I only gave them your name so nobody had to stand here doing forms twice. It wasn't some contract. If you'd said something earlier, I wouldn't have made it sound settled.

messages.speaker: Alex
messages.text: You made it sound settled before I got to the desk. That's the part I'm not doing. Just ask what else is open, and we'll keep it simple.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Wait, not that one. Just give it a second, okay? The whole table's packed, I know, just not that seat.

messages.speaker: Finley
messages.text: It's open, Sam. I'm sitting there. I'm not standing in the aisle balancing a tray while you guard an empty chair.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: I'm not guarding it. Just use the end of the table for a minute. Please not this one.

messages.speaker: Finley
messages.text: The end of the table is where people keep bumping past with backpacks. This seat is here, it's empty, and that's usually how chairs work.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Lower your voice. People are already looking over. Just wait a second and it'll make sense.

messages.speaker: Finley
messages.text: Then say what I'm supposed to be waiting for. You don't get to claim a chair that's empty and expect everyone else to play along.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: I'm asking for one minute, not the whole lunch period. Why is that such a problem?

messages.speaker: Finley
messages.text: Because you do this thing where you make a rule and act like I'm the problem for noticing it. If there's a reason, use words.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: I am using words. I'm saying don't take this seat yet. That's not complicated.

messages.speaker: Finley
messages.text: No, that's an order with no explanation. And with half the cafeteria watching, it looks like I'm trying to steal a chair when I'm literally holding my lunch and looking at the only spot left.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: You could stop making it a scene. I'm standing right here asking you quietly. Just hold on.

messages.speaker: Finley
messages.text: I'm making it a scene? You're the one planted in front of a chair like it's reserved seating. If there's an actual reason, say it now.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: Riley texted me—they're right behind us with everyone's drinks, and I was saving this seat for them. I kept trying to get you to wait like ten seconds.

messages.speaker: Finley
messages.text: Oh. You could have led with Riley instead of turning this into a standoff over a chair. Fine, keep it open.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: I was trying to, and you were already halfway into the seat. I just needed you to pause, not fight me in front of everybody.

messages.speaker: Finley
messages.text: I wasn't trying to fight you. From where I was standing, it looked like you were blocking me for no reason. Move over a little; I'll stand here till Riley gets in.

messages.speaker: Sam
messages.text: They're there, by the napkins. See the drink carrier? Just take my tray for a second so I can clear space.

messages.speaker: Finley
messages.text: Got it. Next time, say the name first and the mystery second. Here, set the drinks down before someone clips your elbow.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: So. Should we call these midnight coffee runs and parking-lot talks an actual date, or are we pretending the espresso machine makes everything unofficial?

messages.speaker: Kendall
messages.text: You waited until this place got loud enough to hide behind the milk steamer before asking that? That's efficient. What exactly are you asking?

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: I'm asking whether this is the part where normal people admit it's been a date-shaped thing for a while. We already do the bad diner fries, the walks after the library closes, the stupid two a.m. texts.

messages.speaker: Kendall
messages.text: That list sounds suspiciously prepared. It also sounds like evidence for a pattern, not an answer. There's a difference.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: Fine, counselor. Maybe I'm asking whether putting a name on it would make it better or just weird. You have strong opinions about categories.

messages.speaker: Kendall
messages.text: Categories matter when one person uses them to simplify things and the other person has to live inside them. If this is just administrative cleanup, that's not especially flattering.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: Administrative cleanup? That's bleak. I was aiming for slightly less bleak than that.

messages.speaker: Kendall
messages.text: You leaned back like you were asking whether we should split a muffin. Forgive me for not hearing violins.

messages.speaker: Lennox
messages.text: Right, because if I'd leaned in and delivered a speech by the sugar packets, that would've gone over great. You looked like you were about to grade my wording anyway.

messages.speaker: Kendall
